key_insight: Strain controls how neighboring iodine vacancies separate or reconfigure in CsPbI3, with finite-temperature hopping behavior differing from the repulsive interactions found in static calculations.
engineering_relevance: Strain management may help control vacancy migration and defect reconfiguration relevant to halide-perovskite structural stability.
method: Machine-learning molecular dynamics of neighboring iodine vacancies under isotropic and biaxial strain.
Analysis of separation and pair-preserving relay hopping in tilted CsPbI3.
Static interaction calculations using DFT and the SevenNet-0 potential.
evidence_signal: Trajectories show nonmonotonic short-time hopping fractions with strain and orientation-dependent behavior under biaxial compression, while static calculations find repulsive interactions in every examined configuration.
watch_item: Short-time hopping behavior does not establish long-term vacancy-pair stability or device-scale performance.
paper_title: Strain-dependent Dynamics of Interactions of Iodine-vacancy pairs in CsPbI3: A DFT and Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Study
